im-2MfZ.title: Kerb: striped
im-2MfZ.summary: Striped kerbs can sometimes be seen along main roads.

im-4nRh.title: Houses: whitewashed walls and entrance walls
im-4nRh.summary: Whitewashed houses and walls around the entrance are common, a look similar to Ireland.

im-Arok.title: Landmark: airport with big flat field
im-Arok.summary: Ronaldsway Airport is a large, flat, open field with a boundary fence.

im-DCeX.title: Landmark: castle on a small island
im-DCeX.summary: Peel Castle sits on a small island and can be seen from the town of Peel.

im-ONfY.title: Lamp post: small yellow sticker
im-ONfY.summary: A small yellow sticker with two letters is used in southern Onchan. The letters are the road's initials, like SD for Sunningdale Drive.

im-Q2No.title: Lamp post: white sticker, two green numbers
im-Q2No.summary: A small white sticker with two green numbers on lamp posts means Douglas.

im-Sk9u.title: Location: town in a NW-SE valley
im-Sk9u.summary: The town of Laxey sits in a valley that runs north-west to south-east.

im-VIUx.title: Lamp post: all green
im-VIUx.summary: All-green lamp posts are common in Ramsey and Castletown, and rarer in the Malew, Santon and Garff parishes.

im-ZZ1O.title: Landscape: hilly farmland, narrow roads
im-ZZ1O.summary: Hilly farmland with narrow roads running through it.

im-abTT.title: Google car: twig smudge on left of lens
im-abTT.summary: A smudge that looks like a twig sits on the left side of the camera view in the south.

im-btUp.title: Landscape: flat north, mountains to south
im-btUp.summary: In the north the land is very flat compared to the rest, and mountains are usually visible to the south.

im-cEF8.title: Location: island between Britain and Ireland
im-cEF8.summary: A British Crown dependency between Britain and Ireland. For country streaks it counts as the United Kingdom.

differs.how: red strip on plates, Gen 2 camera

im-eKbX.title: Plate: UK style with red strip
im-eKbX.summary: White front and yellow rear plates like the UK, but with a red strip on the left. A red strip means Isle of Man.

differs.how: UK plates have no red strip

im-fUGu.title: Bollard: blue
im-fUGu.summary: Blue bollards are common in towns and built-up areas.

im-hu7c.title: Google car: Gen 2 camera only
im-hu7c.summary: All coverage is the older Gen 2 camera: lower quality, a round blur above and below, and slightly off colours.

im-jTc8.title: Houses: rows of terraced houses
im-jTc8.summary: The largest town is recognised by rows of terraced houses and denser buildings. This is the capital, Douglas.

im-kUjb.title: Lamp post: blue base, small blue sticker
im-kUjb.summary: Lamp posts with a blue base and a small blue sticker cover most of the island, except around Douglas and parts of the northeast and south. The first two letters on the sticker give one of 21 parishes.

im-lysj.title: Sign: coat of arms above the text
im-lysj.summary: Many street signs in Port Erin have the coat of arms placed above the street name.

im-pQGf.title: Plants: gorse with yellow flowers
im-pQGf.summary: Gorse, a bush with bright yellow flowers, is very common. It also grows in rugged parts of the UK and Ireland, like the Scottish Highlands.

im-sQ1O.title: Landscape: mostly hilly
im-sQ1O.summary: The island is mostly hilly, with a few exceptions.

im-smmi.title: Sign: oval coat of arms on street signs
im-smmi.summary: Many street signs in Ramsey carry an oval coat of arms.
